metadata.title: CA Bundle Tracker
metadata.description: Which software ships its own Certificate Authority (CA) bundle and which uses the operating system store, with update paths and remediation after the October 2026 eMudhra intermediate CA compromise.

incident.name: The eMudhra intermediate CA compromise (October 2026)
incident.summary: On 2026-10-17 Mozilla received a report that the private keys of 8 eMudhra intermediate CA certificates were compromised: 6 TLS intermediates trusted by Chrome, Mozilla, Microsoft and Apple, and 2 code-signing intermediates trusted by Microsoft. Mozilla's comment 5 on bug 2083449 states that all 8 private keys were integers less than 256; a later public comment (comment 67) lists the values.

notices.heading: The Sectigo AAA Certificate Services cross-sign path
paragraphs: The compromised intermediates were cross-signed by Sectigo's AAA Certificate Services root. Any store that still trusts AAA for TLS accepts the cross-signed copies even after the emSign roots are gone.

Mozilla removed AAA's websites trust bit in April 2025 (bug 1957685, landed in NSS on 2025-04-16). Mozilla-derived bundles taken before that, such as old certifi copies, still trust it. Apple and Microsoft kept trusting AAA and blocked the intermediates by other means (configuration data and the disallowed CTL).

Example: on Amazon Linux 2023 the `awscli-2-2.33.15` package ships `/usr/lib/python3.9/site-packages/awscli/botocore/cacert.pem` (dated 2026-02-06) containing AAA Certificate Services. AWS removed AAA from the bundle in AWS CLI 2.38.4.

sources.title: Mozilla bug 1957685: remove websites trust bit from AAA Certificate Services
MSRC: Microsoft response to compromised eMudhra CA keys

notices.heading: macOS command-line tools are not covered by Apple's fix
paragraphs: Apple's configuration-data block protects Safari, Mail and apps using Apple's networking frameworks. Tools that read `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` (Apple names curl, git, python3, ruby, perl and openssl) can still accept the certificates until a future macOS update.

Apple's article gives optional steps to remove emSign ECC Root CA - G3 and AAA Certificate Services from `/etc/ssl/cert.pem`. Homebrew's merged `cert.pem` re-imports macOS keychain roots, so check it as well.

notices.heading: How each vendor pushed the block
paragraphs: 2026-10-17: reported to Mozilla at 20:06 UTC; OneCRL entries finished at 22:59 UTC and reached Firefox through Remote Settings the same day. Google shipped a CRLSet blocking the intermediates' public keys at 19:45 UTC.

2026-10-19: Apple began blocking the 12 TLS certificates through configuration data (the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 root followed on 2026-10-23). Google Play services delivered the Android block around 22:00 UTC.
2026-10-20: Microsoft updated the Windows disallowed CTL; Mozilla shipped an unscheduled Firefox Release and ESR build for users without Remote Settings.
2026-10-26 and 2026-10-27: Microsoft's out-of-band Windows update and Edge trust-list change removed 7 certificates; Chrome removed emSign ECC Root CA - G3 from the Chrome Root Store.

sources.title: Google: protecting Chrome and Android users from compromised eMudhra intermediates
MSRC: Microsoft response to compromised eMudhra CA keys

notices.heading: Where fixes arrive last
paragraphs: Android 13 and older without Google Play services: the root store lives on the system partition and changes only with a vendor OS update.
Container images built before the fix keep their bundle until rebuilt; so do Lambda container-image functions and anything with a vendored certifi.
Java applications with a custom `javax.net.ssl.trustStore` or `jssecacerts` file gain nothing from a JDK update.
Binaries built with Rust `webpki-roots` or ESP-IDF's certificate bundle carry the roots compiled in; each one must be rebuilt and redeployed.

glossary.definition: Android Pony EXpress, the container format for updatable Android system modules such as Conscrypt.
Certificate Authority: an entity whose certificate vouches for others.
Common CA Database, shared by the major root programs.
Chrome's pushed list of blocked certificates and public keys, delivered by the component updater.
Firefox's compressed revocation data for all publicly trusted certificates.
Certificate Trust List; Windows downloads one of trusted roots and one of disallowed certificates.
Network Security Services, Mozilla's TLS and certificate library; `certdata.txt` holds its root list.
Mozilla's pushed list of revoked intermediate certificates, delivered over Remote Settings.
Over the air: an update delivered to the device without a cable or reinstall.
Privacy-Enhanced Mail: the base64 text form of a certificate (`-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----`).
SubjectPublicKeyInfo: the public key field of a certificate; blocking by SPKI hash covers every certificate with that key.
Transport Layer Security, the protocol behind HTTPS.
Where software gets the roots it trusts: Bundled, OS store, Fallback, Hybrid, or Configured (no default; the operator supplies a CA file).

sections.title: Browsers
sections.caption: Web browsers: root store, update path and the channel that blocked the eMudhra intermediates.

sections.title: Language runtimes and standard libraries
sections.caption: Runtimes and TLS libraries: default roots and the switches that move them to the OS store.

sections.title: Command-line tools and package managers
sections.caption: Command-line tools: where each reads its roots, per platform where it differs.

sections.title: Server software (as TLS clients)
sections.caption: Servers connecting to TLS upstreams: most use only the CA file you configure.

sections.title: Desktop and Electron apps
sections.caption: Desktop applications built on Electron, WebView2, NSS or the OS.

sections.title: Operating system trust stores
sections.caption: OS trust stores: bundle paths, update commands and pushed block lists.

sections.title: Containers and build environments

sections.title: Embedded and IoT
sections.caption: Firmware-based devices (IoT = Internet of Things): roots are compiled into the image or vendor-managed.

entries.name: Chrome / Chromium
entries.location: Compiled into the browser; updated as a component
entries.update_mechanism: Component updater (typically within 24 hours) and browser releases
entries.override: Locally installed roots are honoured: Windows Local Machine, Current User, Enterprise and Group Policy stores; macOS Default and System keychains
entries.remediation: Nothing to do on a default install: Google pushed a CRLSet blocking the intermediates' public keys on 2026-10-17 (19:45 UTC) and removes emSign ECC Root CA - G3 from the Chrome Root Store from 2026-10-27. Installs with component updates disabled need a browser update.
entries.version_notes: Chrome Root Store used from Chrome 105 on Windows and macOS (default by 108), 114 on Linux and ChromeOS, 114 on Android (default by 115).
entries.notes: iOS Chrome uses the Apple verifier and is outside the Chrome Root Store.

sources.title: Google: protecting Chrome and Android users from compromised eMudhra intermediates

entries.name: Microsoft Edge
entries.bundle_origin: Microsoft Trusted Root Program list with Edge's built-in verifier
entries.location: Compiled into the browser; updated as a component
entries.override: Locally installed roots are still trusted
entries.remediation: Keep component updates enabled: Microsoft delivered a CRLSet update to Edge and WebView2, and removed 7 certificates from Edge's trust list on 2026-10-27.
entries.version_notes: Built-in verifier is the default on Windows and macOS from Edge 112; the `MicrosoftRootStoreEnabled` policy was removed in Edge 115.
entries.notes: Edge on iOS and iPadOS uses the Apple root store and verifier. Microsoft's page says Linux and Android move to the built-in verifier in a future release.

sources.title: MSRC: Microsoft response to compromised eMudhra CA keys

entries.name: Firefox
entries.update_mechanism: OneCRL and intermediate data over Remote Settings (no release needed), plus browser releases
entries.override: `security.enterprise_roots.enabled` (default `true` since Firefox 120; reads OS-added roots on Windows and macOS only)
entries.remediation: Nothing to do with Remote Settings on: Mozilla added the intermediates to OneCRL on 2026-10-17. Profiles with Remote Settings disabled need the unscheduled Release/ESR build of 2026-10-20 or later.
entries.version_notes: Built-in roots module rewritten in Rust in Firefox 108. Enterprise roots on by default from Firefox 120 (before that, only after a man-in-the-middle error).
entries.notes: CRLite revocation checking is on by default on desktop from Firefox 137, and intermediate preloading is on by default in source. Distribution builds can differ: Fedora's Firefox uses system NSS and requires `p11-kit-trust`, so it also sees the OS store.

entries.name: Safari
entries.update_mechanism: Apple certificate configuration data (automatic) and OS updates
entries.remediation: Nothing to do: Apple blocks the 12 TLS certificates through configuration data from 2026-10-19, and the emSign ECC Root CA - G3 root from 2026-10-23.

entries.name: Brave
entries.bundle_origin: Chrome Root Store (unmodified Chromium certificate verifier)
entries.update_mechanism: Browser releases; Brave uses Chrome's CRLSet component
entries.remediation: Keep Brave updated and component updates enabled; check `brave://components` for a current CRLSet.
entries.notes: Brave on iOS uses the Apple store.
entries.unverified_note: Brave documents Chrome's root store and a developer confirms CRLSet use, but no official source says root-store updates arrive by component update, and Brave published no eMudhra statement.

entries.name: Opera
entries.remediation: Keep Opera updated.
entries.unverified_note: Opera states it trusts the Chrome Root Store; how (or whether) it receives root-store or CRLSet updates between releases is not documented.

entries.name: Vivaldi
entries.bundle_origin: Chromium certificate verifier (assumed Chrome Root Store)
entries.remediation: Keep Vivaldi updated.
entries.unverified_note: No official Vivaldi source describes its root store or CRLSet handling.

sources.title: Vivaldi blog (no root store statement found)

entries.name: Tor Browser
entries.remediation: Update Tor Browser: its base profile disables Remote Settings intermediates, CRLite and enterprise roots, so the OneCRL push may not reach it before a release.
entries.notes: Checked in the `tor-browser-140.0esr-15.0-1` profile: CRLite mode 0, intermediate preloading off.

entries.name: Arc
entries.bundle_origin: Chromium certificate verifier (assumed Chrome Root Store)
entries.remediation: Plan a move: Arc is reported to end on 2026-12-22; until then keep it updated.
entries.unverified_note: No official Browser Company source on Arc's root store or CRLSet handling; the end-of-life date comes from press coverage.

entries.name: Python (requests / certifi)
entries.bundle_origin: Mozilla roots repackaged by the certifi project
entries.location: `certifi/cacert.pem` in site-packages (`python -m certifi` prints the path)
entries.override: `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, then `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`; `verify=` per call. requests does not read `SSL_CERT_FILE`.
entries.remediation: Upgrade certifi in every virtual environment, image and vendored copy, or set `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` to the patched OS bundle.
entries.notes: The environment variables apply when `trust_env` is on (the default for `requests.get`).

entries.name: Python (standard library ssl)
entries.location: OpenSSL default paths (`ssl.get_default_verify_paths()`); on Windows also the system ROOT and CA stores
entries.remediation: Update the OS trust store. See the python.org macOS row for the installer build.

entries.name: Python (python.org macOS installer)
entries.location: certifi in the framework's site-packages, installed by `Install Certificates.command`
entries.remediation: Re-run `/Applications/Python 3.x/Install Certificates.command` after certifi publishes a fixed bundle. Apple's configuration-data fix does not reach this OpenSSL.
entries.notes: The python.org build ships its own OpenSSL and does not read the macOS keychain.

entries.name: Node.js (official builds)
entries.override: `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` adds a PEM file; `--use-system-ca` or `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` adds the OS store; `--use-openssl-ca` replaces the bundle with the OpenSSL default paths (`SSL_CERT_FILE` / `SSL_CERT_DIR`), not the Windows or macOS store
entries.remediation: Upgrade Node.js to a release with current bundled roots, or run with `--use-system-ca` so OS fixes apply.
entries.version_notes: `--use-system-ca`: v23.8.0, v22.15.0. `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1`: v24.6.0, v22.19.0 (the flag wins if both are set). `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`: v7.3.0.
entries.notes: `--use-system-ca` reads the Windows and macOS stores directly; elsewhere (v23.9.0+) it reads the OpenSSL file and directory.

entries.name: Java (upstream OpenJDK builds)
entries.remediation: Update the JDK, and look for custom `javax.net.ssl.trustStore` files and `jssecacerts`, which a JDK update does not touch.

entries.name: Java (Linux distribution JDKs)
entries.bundle_origin: Regenerated from the OS trust store
entries.remediation: Update the OS `ca-certificates` package; on Debian run `update-ca-certificates -f` if the Java keystore did not refresh.

entries.name: Go (standard library)
entries.bundle_origin: OS store; roots from `golang.org/x/crypto/x509roots/fallback` only when the OS provides none
entries.location: Linux: first existing of `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`, `/etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt`, `/etc/ssl/ca-bundle.pem`, ... plus `/etc/ssl/certs`; Windows and macOS: platform verifier
entries.update_mechanism: OS update (primary); module update and rebuild (fallback roots)
entries.remediation: Update the OS store. Binaries that import `x509roots/fallback` and run without system roots (for example in `scratch` images) need a rebuild with a newer module.
entries.version_notes: Go 1.20 added fallback roots. Go 1.27 honours `SSL_CERT_FILE` / `SSL_CERT_DIR` on Windows and macOS too, and then uses the Go verifier instead of the platform one (`GODEBUG=x509sslcertoverrideplatform=0` restores the old behaviour).

entries.name: Rust (webpki-roots crate)
entries.bundle_origin: Mozilla roots from the Common CA Database (CCADB) at crate release
entries.remediation: Rebuild every binary with a current webpki-roots and redeploy it.

entries.name: Rust (rustls-native-certs)
entries.location: Windows system store; macOS keychain trust settings; Linux / Unix bundle found by `openssl-probe`
entries.remediation: Update the OS store. Only root changes reach it: it loads roots into rustls, so OS intermediate block lists are not applied.
entries.notes: The crate's README now recommends `rustls-platform-verifier`.

entries.name: Rust (rustls-platform-verifier)
entries.location: Windows, macOS, iOS, Android: platform verifier; Linux: webpki with the system bundle
entries.remediation: Update the OS; OS-delivered blocks apply where the platform verifier is used.

entries.name: Dart / Flutter
entries.bundle_origin: OS store; compiled-in roots as a last resort on Linux
entries.location: Linux: first existing of `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`, `/etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt`, ...; Android: `/apex/com.android.conscrypt/cacerts`, else `/system/etc/security/cacerts`; Windows: ROOT and CA system stores; macOS / iOS: platform trust
entries.update_mechanism: OS update; SDK release for the compiled-in fallback
entries.remediation: Update the OS store. On Linux hosts with no system bundle, update the Dart SDK or Flutter engine.
entries.notes: The API page says Linux and Windows use Mozilla's list; the VM source reads the system stores first. This row follows the source.

entries.name: Deno
entries.remediation: Upgrade Deno, or set `DENO_TLS_CA_STORE=system` so OS fixes apply.

entries.name: Bun
entries.override: `--use-system-ca` or `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` adds the OS store; `SSL_CERT_FILE` / `SSL_CERT_DIR` add certificates; `--use-openssl-ca` uses only the OpenSSL paths
entries.remediation: Upgrade Bun, or run with `--use-system-ca`.

entries.name: Ruby (openssl extension)
entries.remediation: Update the OS trust store (on macOS, see the `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` notice).
entries.notes: RubyGems adds one shipped root for rubygems.org (`lib/rubygems/ssl_certs`) on top of the OpenSSL defaults.

entries.name: PHP
entries.location: Unix: OpenSSL default paths; Windows: Windows certificate verification callback (stream TLS)
entries.remediation: Update the OS store; check `php.ini` for a stale `openssl.cafile` or `curl.cainfo` bundle.
entries.unverified_note: The Windows stream-TLS behaviour comes from php-src source only, and the ext/curl default on Windows when neither ini value is set is undocumented.

entries.name: .NET / C#
entries.location: Windows / macOS: platform verifier; Linux: OpenSSL default paths, falling back to `/etc/ssl/certs`
entries.remediation: Update the OS trust store.

entries.name: Perl (IO::Socket::SSL)
entries.bundle_origin: OS store; `Mozilla::CA` only when no usable system default is found
entries.remediation: Update the OS store; also update `Mozilla::CA` on hosts that fall back to it.

entries.name: Erlang/OTP
entries.bundle_origin: OS store when the application asks for it
entries.remediation: Update the OS store. Applications that pass the hex `certifi` package's file instead carry a bundled Mozilla copy and need a dependency update.
entries.notes: OTP loads no roots by itself: `ssl` needs `{cacerts, public_key:cacerts_get()}` or `cacertfile`. The `certifi` package is a hex / rebar3 dependency, not part of OTP.

entries.name: Swift
entries.location: Apple: Security.framework (`SecTrust`); Linux: system PEM bundle (swift-nio-ssl with BoringSSL; Foundation via libcurl)
entries.remediation: Update the OS trust store.

entries.name: curl (macOS system)
entries.remediation: Apple's configuration-data block does not cover this file. Until a macOS update fixes it, follow Apple's optional steps to remove emSign ECC Root CA - G3 and AAA Certificate Services from `/etc/ssl/cert.pem`, or pass `--cacert` with a clean bundle.
entries.version_notes: Upstream curl removed Secure Transport in 8.15.0; `--ca-native` (use the OS store with OpenSSL-family backends) arrived in 8.2.0.

entries.name: curl (Windows system)
entries.override: `--cacert` with a file-based backend only; `--ca-native` has no effect with Schannel
entries.remediation: Nothing beyond Windows Update.
entries.version_notes: Upstream curl removed Secure Transport in 8.15.0; `--ca-native` (use the OS store with OpenSSL-family backends) arrived in 8.2.0.

sources.title: curl: the curl shipped by Microsoft

entries.name: curl (Linux distributions)
entries.remediation: Update the OS `ca-certificates` package.
entries.version_notes: Upstream curl removed Secure Transport in 8.15.0; `--ca-native` (use the OS store with OpenSSL-family backends) arrived in 8.2.0.

entries.name: curl (Homebrew)
entries.bundle_origin: Homebrew OpenSSL default bundle (macOS: also Apple SecTrust)
entries.remediation: Run `brew upgrade ca-certificates curl`.
entries.unverified_note: The formula builds with `--with-ca-fallback` and, on macOS, `--with-apple-sectrust`; the effective default is inferred from those flags and not documented in one place.

entries.name: OpenSSL (Homebrew openssl@3 / openssl@4)
entries.bundle_origin: Merged bundle: macOS System and SystemRootCertificates keychains (Linux: the first system bundle found) plus the Mozilla list
entries.location: `$(brew --prefix)/etc/openssl@3/cert.pem` links to `$(brew --prefix)/etc/ca-certificates/cert.pem`; the Mozilla-only copy is `$(brew --prefix)/share/ca-certificates/cacert.pem`
entries.update_mechanism: `brew upgrade ca-certificates` (post-install regenerates the merged file)
entries.remediation: Run `brew upgrade ca-certificates`, then scan the merged `cert.pem`: it re-imports macOS keychain roots, and the macOS keychain still holds AAA Certificate Services.
entries.notes: The formula's Mozilla copy (curl.se `cacert-2026-10-20`) excludes AAA Certificate Services and the emSign G3 roots by public-key hash.

entries.name: Homebrew (`brew` itself)
entries.bundle_origin: System curl and Homebrew's Portable Ruby
entries.remediation: On macOS, downloads go through system curl and `/etc/ssl/cert.pem`; see the macOS command-line notice.
entries.notes: Homebrew uses Portable Ruby unless the system Ruby is new enough, and uses brewed curl only when no suitable system curl exists (`HOMEBREW_FORCE_BREWED_CURL` is then set automatically).

entries.name: wget (GNU)
entries.location: Paths chosen when OpenSSL was installed
entries.remediation: Update the OS store.

entries.name: git
entries.location: Linux: libcurl's compiled-in bundle; macOS: `/etc/ssl/cert.pem`; Git for Windows: Windows store (Schannel, installer default) or `mingw64/etc/ssl/certs/ca-bundle.crt` (OpenSSL option)
entries.update_mechanism: OS update; Git for Windows release for the OpenSSL bundle
entries.remediation: Update the OS store. On macOS see the `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` notice; Git for Windows with the OpenSSL backend needs a Git for Windows update.

entries.name: pip
entries.bundle_origin: OS store via the vendored truststore, plus vendored certifi
entries.override: `--cert`, `PIP_CERT`, `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE`, `CURL_CA_BUNDLE`; opt out of the OS store with `--use-deprecated=legacy-certs`
entries.remediation: Upgrade pip (the vendored certifi copy is still trusted alongside the OS store) and update the OS store.
entries.version_notes: pip 24.2+ on Python 3.10+ uses the OS store in addition to certifi by default. pip 22.2 to 24.1 needed `--use-feature=truststore`.

entries.name: npm / yarn
entries.remediation: Upgrade Node.js, or set `NODE_USE_SYSTEM_CA=1` for npm and yarn.

entries.name: cargo
entries.remediation: Update the OS store.
entries.notes: Cargo's HTTP client is libcurl; the docs say it uses the system certificates when `http.cainfo` is not set.

entries.name: rustup
entries.remediation: Update the OS store.
entries.notes: Default download backend is reqwest with rustls and `rustls-platform-verifier`; the curl backend is deprecated since rustup 1.28.2.

entries.name: docker CLI and Engine
entries.location: Linux: Go's bundle search; registry CAs under `/etc/docker/certs.d/` are merged with system roots
entries.remediation: Update the OS store.

sources.title: Docker: verify repository client with certificates

entries.name: kubectl
entries.bundle_origin: Cluster CA from kubeconfig; otherwise OS store (Go)
entries.remediation: Usually nothing: clusters normally pin their own CA in kubeconfig.

entries.name: Terraform / OpenTofu
entries.remediation: Update the OS store.
entries.unverified_note: Neither HashiCorp nor OpenTofu documents the CA source; the row assumes Go's default system roots.

entries.name: AWS CLI v2
entries.remediation: Upgrade to 2.38.4 or later. Where a distribution package lags (Amazon Linux 2023 `awscli-2-2.33.15` still contains AAA), set `AWS_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/pki/tls/certs/ca-bundle.crt`.
entries.version_notes: 2.38.4 removed AAA Certificate Services from the vendored bundle (eMudhra cross-sign). 2.39.3 is the current release.
entries.notes: The Amazon Linux 2023 path and its AAA Certificate Services entry were observed on an `awscli-2-2.33.15-1.amzn2023.0.1` host (bundle dated 2026-02-06).

entries.name: Google Cloud CLI (gcloud)
entries.remediation: Run `gcloud components update`, or set `core/custom_ca_certs_file` to the OS bundle.
entries.notes: Path checked in the official 591.0.0 Linux tarball.

entries.name: Azure CLI (az)
entries.location: Windows: `C:\Program Files\Microsoft SDKs\Azure\CLI2\Lib\site-packages\certifi\cacert.pem`; Debian / Ubuntu: `/opt/az/lib/python<version>/site-packages/certifi/cacert.pem`; RHEL / SUSE: `/usr/lib64/az/lib/python<version>/site-packages/certifi/cacert.pem`
entries.remediation: Update the Azure CLI, or set `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` to the OS bundle.

entries.name: apt
entries.remediation: Update `ca-certificates`.
entries.version_notes: apt 2.9.19 replaced GnuTLS with OpenSSL (Debian 13 ships apt 3.0; Debian 12 ships 2.6 with GnuTLS).

entries.name: dnf / yum
entries.remediation: Update `ca-certificates`.

entries.name: nginx (proxy to TLS upstreams)
entries.update_mechanism: Whoever maintains that file; an OS update fixes it when it points at the OS bundle
entries.remediation: Check that `proxy_ssl_verify` is on and that `proxy_ssl_trusted_certificate` points at an updated bundle.
entries.notes: `proxy_ssl_verify` is off by default, so upstream certificates are not checked at all unless enabled.

entries.name: Apache httpd (mod_ssl proxy)
entries.remediation: Check that `SSLProxyVerify` is `require` and the proxy CA file is current.
entries.notes: `SSLProxyVerify` defaults to `none`. `SSLCACertificateFile` is for authenticating clients, not upstreams.

entries.name: HAProxy
entries.location: `ca-file` on each `server` line; `@system-ca` selects the OS store
entries.update_mechanism: Whoever maintains the file; OS update when `@system-ca` is used
entries.remediation: Use `ca-file @system-ca` and update the OS store, or refresh the configured CA file.
entries.version_notes: `@system-ca` is first documented in the HAProxy 2.6 manual.
entries.notes: Server certificate verification is required by default (`ssl-server-verify`). The built-in HTTP client defaults to `@system-ca`.

entries.name: Envoy
entries.override: `trusted_ca` (often pointed at the OS bundle, for example `/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`)
entries.remediation: Make sure every upstream cluster sets `trusted_ca`, and refresh the file it names.
entries.notes: Without `trusted_ca`, a presented peer certificate is not verified.

entries.name: Caddy (reverse proxy)
entries.remediation: Update the OS store, or the file named by `tls_trust_pool file`.
entries.notes: The system-pool default comes from Caddy's source (no CA configured leaves Go's `RootCAs` unset).

entries.name: Traefik
entries.remediation: Update the OS store, or the files listed in `rootCAs`.
entries.unverified_note: Traefik's documentation gives `rootCAs` a default of `[]` but does not say that an empty list means the system pool; that follows from Go's TLS client.

entries.name: PostgreSQL (libpq clients)
entries.remediation: Use `sslmode=verify-full`; refresh `root.crt` or switch to `sslrootcert=system`.
entries.notes: The default `sslmode=prefer` does not verify the server. `ssl_ca_file` is a server setting for client certificates.

entries.name: MySQL / MariaDB clients
entries.remediation: Set `--ssl-ca` to an updated bundle and use `VERIFY_IDENTITY`.
entries.notes: MySQL 8.4 clients do not authenticate the server without `--ssl-ca` / `--ssl-capath` (default mode `PREFERRED`). MariaDB Connector/C 3.4 verifies server certificates by default.
entries.unverified_note: Which CA source MariaDB Connector/C 3.4 uses when none is configured is not documented on the pages checked.

entries.name: VS Code
entries.bundle_origin: Chromium verifier for the workbench; OS certificates added to the extension host
entries.remediation: Update VS Code and the OS store; leave `http.systemCertificates` on.
entries.notes: The `http.systemCertificates` setting and its default appear in VS Code's source; the network page says the Chromium stack uses the OS trust infrastructure.

entries.name: Electron apps (general)
entries.bundle_origin: Chromium verifier for `net` and web content; Node.js bundled roots for Node `https` in the main process
entries.location: Compiled into the app's Electron and Node.js binaries
entries.remediation: Update the app; ask the vendor which Electron version it ships.
entries.unverified_note: Electron's docs say `net` uses Chromium's network stack, but do not state which root store its Chromium build uses or that main-process Node `https` keeps Node's bundled roots.

entries.name: Slack desktop
entries.remediation: Keep Slack updated.
entries.unverified_note: Slack publishes no statement on certificate trust; the row assumes stock Electron behaviour.

entries.name: Discord desktop
entries.remediation: Keep Discord updated.
entries.unverified_note: Discord publishes no statement on certificate trust; the row assumes stock Electron behaviour.

entries.name: Microsoft Teams (new)
entries.remediation: Keep the WebView2 runtime updated: Microsoft says its CRLSet update covers Edge and WebView2.
entries.unverified_note: Microsoft documents that Teams requires WebView2 but not that WebView2 uses Edge's built-in verifier and trust list.

entries.name: Thunderbird
entries.remediation: Update Thunderbird.
entries.notes: Thunderbird's profile does not override the Gecko enterprise-roots, CRLite or intermediate-preloading defaults.
entries.unverified_note: Whether Thunderbird applies OneCRL updates between releases is not documented.

entries.name: Outlook (classic, Windows)
entries.remediation: Nothing beyond Windows Update.

entries.remediation: Keep the WebView2 runtime updated.
entries.unverified_note: Microsoft documents that new Outlook uses WebView2 but not which verifier WebView2 applies.

entries.name: Zoom desktop
entries.override: Add intercepting-proxy roots to the OS trusted root store
entries.remediation: Update the OS store.
entries.notes: Zoom's support article tells users to fix untrusted-issuer errors in the system trusted root store. Linux behaviour is not documented.

entries.name: macOS
entries.location: Trust anchors and `TrustStore.html` in `/System/Library/Security/Certificates.bundle`; `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` for LibreSSL command-line tools
entries.update_mechanism: Trust-store assets fetched by `trustd` (checked every 12 hours) and OS updates
entries.remediation: Nothing for apps using Apple's frameworks. Command-line tools reading `/etc/ssl/cert.pem` need the steps in the macOS notice.

sources.title: Apple: trust store for the 26 OS releases

entries.name: iOS / iPadOS
entries.update_mechanism: Apple configuration data and OS updates
entries.remediation: Nothing to do.

entries.name: Windows
entries.location: System certificate stores; `authrootstl.cab` (trusted roots) and `disallowedcertstl.cab` (untrusted certificates) from `ctldl.windowsupdate.com`
entries.update_mechanism: Certificate trust lists (CTLs) downloaded daily by connected machines, plus Windows Update
entries.remediation: Nothing on connected machines. Disconnected machines need the CTL files deployed by an administrator.
entries.notes: Microsoft updated the disallowed CTL on 2026-10-20 and shipped an out-of-band Windows update on 2026-10-26 that removes 7 certificates from the Windows trust list.

sources.title: Microsoft Learn: configure trusted roots and disallowed certificates

entries.name: Debian / Ubuntu
entries.remediation: Upgrade `ca-certificates`; rebuild images derived from older bases.

entries.name: RHEL / Fedora / CentOS Stream
entries.remediation: Upgrade `ca-certificates`, or add the certificates to `/etc/pki/ca-trust/source/blocklist/` and run `update-ca-trust`.

entries.name: Amazon Linux 2023
entries.remediation: Upgrade `ca-certificates`; also check bundled copies such as the `awscli-2` RPM.
entries.notes: Layout observed on an Amazon Linux 2023.11 host (`ca-certificates-2025.2.76`), whose bundle contains no AAA Certificate Services.
entries.unverified_note: No Amazon documentation of the bundle paths was found; the paths come from a live host.

entries.name: Alpine Linux
entries.remediation: Upgrade `ca-certificates` and rebuild Alpine-based images.

entries.name: Arch Linux
entries.remediation: Run `pacman -Syu`.

entries.name: SUSE / openSUSE
entries.remediation: Update the CA packages.

entries.name: NixOS
entries.remediation: Update the channel and rebuild.

entries.name: Android
entries.update_mechanism: Android 14+: Google Play system updates (Mainline); older: vendor OS update only
entries.remediation: Keep Google Play services and Google Play system updates current. Devices without Google Play services that run Android 13 or older depend on vendor updates.
entries.notes: Google pushed an equivalent block through Google Play services around 22:00 UTC on Monday 2026-10-19 (the blog gives the weekday; the date follows from the 2026-10-17 report).

sources.title: Google: protecting Chrome and Android users from compromised eMudhra intermediates

entries.name: ChromeOS
entries.update_mechanism: ChromeOS auto-update and Chrome component updater
entries.remediation: Nothing for the browser.
entries.unverified_note: The Chrome Root Store covers the Chrome browser on ChromeOS from Chrome 114; whether system services and Android or Linux apps on ChromeOS use it is not documented.

entries.name: FreeBSD
entries.remediation: Run `freebsd-update fetch install` and `pkg upgrade ca_root_nss`.

entries.name: Container images (Debian, Ubuntu, Alpine bases)
entries.remediation: Rebuild from an updated base image, or run `apt-get update && apt-get install -y ca-certificates` (Alpine: `apk upgrade ca-certificates`) in the build.
entries.notes: An image's files do not change after it is built; a running container keeps the bundle it was built with.

entries.name: distroless images
entries.update_mechanism: Image rebuild from a new distroless digest
entries.remediation: Rebuild from the current distroless image digest.

entries.name: scratch images (static Go / Rust binaries)
entries.bundle_origin: Whatever the build copies in, or roots compiled into the binary
entries.remediation: Rebuild with an updated copied bundle, Go fallback module or webpki-roots crate.

entries.name: GitHub-hosted Actions runners
entries.update_mechanism: Provider image updates (weekly cadence, 2-3 day rollout)
entries.remediation: Nothing for hosted runners beyond the next image; self-hosted runners and job containers need their own updates.

entries.name: AWS Lambda managed runtimes
entries.bundle_origin: The language runtime's own bundle inside the managed runtime
entries.location: Runtime image; `/var/runtime/ca-cert.pem` holds extra Amazon CAs only
entries.update_mechanism: Automatic runtime updates by AWS (default mode)
entries.override: `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/var/runtime/ca-cert.pem` restores the Node.js 18 behaviour on Node.js 20+
entries.remediation: Keep the runtime update mode on Auto. Functions that vendor certifi or their own bundle, and container-image functions, need a redeploy or rebuild.
entries.version_notes: From Node.js 20, Lambda no longer loads the extra Amazon CAs by default.

entries.name: Google Cloud Run (source deployments)
entries.update_mechanism: Automatic base image updates, when enabled
entries.remediation: Enable automatic base image updates, or redeploy.
entries.notes: Without automatic base image updates the bundle changes only on redeploy.

sources.title: Cloud Run: automatic base image updates

entries.name: ESP-IDF (ESP32 family)
entries.bundle_origin: Mozilla NSS root list (full, or a filtered subset of about 35)
entries.update_mechanism: Firmware update over the air (OTA), or `esp_crt_bundle_set()` at runtime
entries.override: `CONFIG_MBEDTLS_CUSTOM_CERTIFICATE_BUNDLE_PATH` adds certificates to the default bundle; `esp_crt_bundle_set()` replaces it at runtime
entries.remediation: Rebuild firmware with the current bundle and ship it over the air, or push a new bundle through `esp_crt_bundle_set()`.

entries.name: Cisco IOS / IOS XE
entries.bundle_origin: Cisco built-in CAs and the Cisco Trusted Root Store bundle
entries.update_mechanism: Automatic trustpool update from Cisco (`cabundle url`), or software update
entries.override: `crypto pki trustpool policy` / `cabundle url`; `crypto pki trustpool import url`
entries.remediation: Import the current Cisco bundle with `crypto pki trustpool import url` or check that automatic updates are enabled.

sources.title: Cisco IOS XE: PKI trustpool management

entries.name: Fortinet FortiOS
entries.remediation: Check that the FortiGuard certificate bundle is current.
entries.notes: Source is a Fortinet-run community technical tip rather than the administration guide.

sources.title: Fortinet community: certificate bundle updates via FortiGuard

entries.name: Juniper Junos OS
entries.update_mechanism: Automatic download from Juniper's content delivery network (default)
entries.remediation: Check that the dynamic trusted-CA update has run.

sources.title: Junos OS: dynamic update of trusted CA bundles

entries.name: Smart TVs / set-top boxes
entries.update_mechanism: Firmware update, if the vendor ships one
entries.remediation: Apply vendor firmware updates; there is usually no user-side fix.
entries.unverified_note: Generalisation without a vendor source; embedded TLS stacks such as wolfSSL load CA certificates from compiled-in buffers.

sources.title: wolfSSL manual: certificate and key APIs

entries.name: Automotive (infotainment / telematics)
entries.location: Head-unit or telematics control unit (TCU) firmware
entries.remediation: Apply manufacturer updates.
entries.unverified_note: Generalisation without a manufacturer source.

sources.title: wolfSSL manual: certificate and key APIs

entries.name: Industrial controllers (PLCs, HMIs)
entries.remediation: Apply vendor firmware updates; isolate devices that cannot be updated.
entries.unverified_note: Generalisation without a vendor source. PLC = programmable logic controller; HMI = human-machine interface.

sources.title: wolfSSL manual: certificate and key APIs
